qa.e: 7s: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35. 35 ends in 5, so it is in the 5s too.

qa.q: Counting by 5s and by 7s up to 100, which two numbers are common?
qa.e: From the 7s, only 35 and 70 end in 5 or 0.

qa.q: Counting by 2s and by 5s, what is the first number in both?
qa.e: 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. 5s: 5, 10. The first common number is 10.

qa.q: Sonu counts in 2s starting from 4. Will he say 17?
qa.a: No, he only says even numbers
qa.e: 4, 6, 8 ... 16, 18. Every number is even, so 17 never comes.

qa.q: Counting in 10s from 10, which of these will you say?
qa.e: 10s from 10 give numbers ending in 0. 100 comes.

qa.q: Counting in 5s from 5, which number will you land on?
qa.e: 5s land on numbers ending in 5 or 0. 65 ends in 5.

qa.q: Mira counts on in 2s from 20: 22, 24, 26 ... Will she say 18?
qa.e: Counting on only goes up from 20. 18 is less than 20.

qa.q: Counting in 3s from 1 (1, 4, 7 ...), which number will you land on?
Counting in 2s from 2, which number will you never say?
qa.e: Counting in 2s from 2 gives even numbers. 35 is odd.

qa.q: Count backward: 10, 9, 8, 7, ___
qa.e: Each number is 1 less. 7 - 1 = 6.

qa.q: Count back in 3s: 21, 18, 15, ___
qa.e: Take away 3 each time. 15 - 3 = 12.

qa.q: Count back in 20s: 100, 80, 60, ___
qa.e: Take away 20 each time. 60 - 20 = 40.

qa.q: Pinky counts back from 20 to 0 in twos. How many steps does she take?
Which list shows counting back in 5s?
qa.e: 60, 55, 50, 45 takes away 5 every time.

qa.q: Fix the pattern of counting back in 10s: 40, 30, 25, 10. What should replace 25?
qa.e: Counting back in 10s from 30 gives 20. So 40, 30, 20, 10.

qa.q: Which number comes just before 30?
qa.e: 1 less than 30 is 29.

qa.q: 9, 19, 29, 39, ___. What comes next?
qa.e: Each number is 10 more. 39 + 10 = 49.

qa.q: On the 100 chart, where are 9, 19, 29, 39 ... 99?
qa.e: They all end in 9, so they sit one under another in the same column.

qa.q: The slanting pattern goes 1, 12, 23, 34. How much is added each time?
Continue the slanting pattern: 56, 67, 78, ___
qa.e: Add 11 each time. 78 + 11 = 89.

qa.q: Rohan colours 5, 15, 25, 35 on the chart. How can we describe this pattern?
qa.a: Each is 10 more than the one before
qa.e: 15 - 5 = 10, 25 - 15 = 10. Each number is 10 more.

qa.q: On a 100 chart, which number is just below 34?
qa.e: Just below means 10 more. 34 + 10 = 44.

qa.q: On a 100 chart, which number is just above 58?
qa.e: Just above means 10 less. 58 - 10 = 48.

qa.q: On a 100 chart, which number is just to the right of 79?
qa.e: Right means 1 more. 79 + 1 = 80.

qa.q: On a 100 chart, which number is just to the left of 63?
qa.e: Left means 1 less. 63 - 1 = 62.

qa.q: A window from the chart has 26 in the middle. What is just below 26?
qa.e: Below is 10 more. 26 + 10 = 36.

qa.q: A chart window shows 14, 15 on top and 24, ___ below. What is missing?
qa.e: The missing box is below 15, so it is 15 + 10 = 25. It is also right of 24.

qa.q: A pattern grows: 1, 3, 5 blocks. How many blocks in the next shape?
qa.e: Each step adds 2 blocks. 5 + 2 = 7.

qa.q: A staircase pattern has 1, 2, 3, 4 blocks. How many blocks are added each time?
qa.e: Each step is 1 block taller: 2 - 1 = 1.

qa.q: A square pattern has 1, then 4, then 9 blocks. How many blocks make 3 rows of 3?
qa.e: 3 rows of 3 is 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

qa.q: Square pattern: 1, 4, 9. The next square has 4 rows of 4. How many blocks?
Sapna adds 3 blocks each time: 3, 6, 9. How many in the next shape?
A tower pattern has 2, 4, 6, 8 blocks. How many blocks in the 5th tower?
qa.e: Each tower has 2 more. The 4th has 8, so the 5th has 10.

qa.q: When does a shadow form?
qa.e: An object stops the light. The dark patch behind it is the shadow.

qa.q: Mona switches off every light in her room at night. What happens to her shadow?
qa.e: A shadow needs light. With no light, there is no shadow.

qa.q: Abu moves a torch closer to his toy elephant. What happens to its shadow on the wall?
qa.e: When the torch comes closer, the toy blocks more light, so the shadow grows.

qa.q: At what time of day is your shadow the shortest?
qa.e: At noon the sun is high overhead, so the shadow is short.

qa.q: Which of these makes a shadow in the sun?
qa.e: A tree is a thing that blocks sunlight, so it makes a shadow.

qa.q: Rani sees that her shadow is very long. What time is it most likely?
qa.e: Shadows are long when the sun is low, in the early morning or evening.

qa.q: Riya draws around the bottom of a juice can. What shape does she get?
qa.e: The bottom of a can is round. Drawing around it gives a circle.

qa.q: Arjun draws around one face of a dice. What shape does he get?
qa.e: Every face of a dice has 4 equal sides. That is a square.

qa.q: Meena draws around the long face of a brick. What shape does she get?
qa.e: The long face has 2 long sides and 2 short sides. That is a rectangle.

qa.q: Kabir shines a torch on a ball. What shape is its shadow on the wall?
qa.e: A ball is round, so its shadow is a round circle.

qa.q: Which solid shape can make a triangle shadow from the side?
qa.e: A party cap is a cone. From the side it has a pointed top and a flat bottom, like a triangle.

qa.q: Which thing has a face you can draw around to get a square?
qa.e: A dice is a cube. Each of its faces is a square.

qa.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
qa.e: Tri means three. A triangle has 3 straight sides.

qa.q: How many corners does a circle have?
qa.e: A circle is round all the way. It has no corners at all.

qa.q: A samosa lying flat on a plate looks like a ___.
qa.e: A samosa has 3 pointy corners and 3 sides, like a triangle.

qa.q: Which of these looks like a circle?
qa.e: A bangle is round with no corners, like a circle.

qa.q: Aisha drew a shape with 3 straight sides. What did she draw?
qa.e: A shape with 3 straight sides is a triangle.

qa.q: How many corners do 2 triangles have in all?
qa.e: Each triangle has 3 corners. 3 + 3 = 6.

qa.q: How many sides does a square have?
qa.e: A square has 4 straight sides, all the same length.

qa.q: What is special about the 4 sides of a square?
qa.a: They are all the same length
qa.e: All 4 sides of a square are equal. That is what makes it a square.

qa.q: A classroom door looks like a ___.
qa.e: A door has 4 sides: 2 long and 2 short. That is a rectangle.

qa.q: How many corners does a rectangle have?
qa.e: A rectangle has 4 corners, one at each end of its sides.

qa.q: Joseph plays carrom. The carrom board looks like a ___.
qa.e: A carrom board has 4 equal sides and 4 corners. It is a square.

qa.q: How many corners do 1 square and 1 triangle have in all?
qa.e: A square has 4 corners and a triangle has 3. 4 + 3 = 7.

qa.q: A rangoli has 3 circles, 4 triangles and 2 squares. How many triangles?
qa.e: The rangoli has 4 triangles. 3 are circles and 2 are squares.

qa.q: A rangoli has 3 circles, 4 triangles and 2 squares. How many shapes in all?
Tia colours every triangle red and every circle blue in her design. Why does this help?
qa.a: She can count each shape easily
qa.e: Each colour shows one kind of shape, so she can count them quickly.

qa.q: Kunal makes a wall hanging with 5 paper triangles and 3 paper circles. How many cut-outs did he use?
qa.e: 5 + 3 = 8 cut-outs.

qa.q: Which shape has 4 sides, two long and two short?
qa.e: A rectangle has 4 sides. Opposite sides match: 2 long and 2 short.

qa.q: A design has 6 squares. Rina colours 2 of them yellow. How many squares are not yellow?
qa.e: 6 - 2 = 4 squares are not yellow.

qa.q: Priya makes her own design with 2 circles, 3 triangles and 1 square. How many different kinds of shapes did she use?
qa.e: The kinds are circle, triangle and square. That is 3 kinds, even though there are 6 shapes.

qa.q: Where is a corner formed?
qa.e: A corner is the point where two straight edges meet.

qa.q: How many corners does a rectangle table top have?
qa.e: A rectangle has 4 straight edges and 4 corners.

qa.q: How many corners does a round roti have?
qa.e: A roti is round. Its edge is curved, so it has no corners.

qa.q: Which object has only a curved edge?
qa.e: A coin is round. The others have straight edges.

qa.q: Which object has both straight and curved edges?
qa.e: A gas cylinder has straight sides and curved edges at the top and bottom.

qa.q: One child stands at each corner of 2 square mats. How many children?
qa.e: Each square has 4 corners. 4 + 4 = 8 children.

qa.q: How many corners does a square sheet of paper have?
qa.e: A square has 4 corners.

qa.q: Tina folds a square paper from corner to corner. What shape does she get?
qa.e: Folding corner to corner makes a triangle.

qa.q: How many edges does the folded paper triangle have?
qa.e: A triangle has 3 edges and 3 corners.

qa.q: Fold a square corner to corner both ways, then open it. How many small triangles do you see?
qa.e: The two folds cross in the middle and make 4 small triangles.

qa.q: Meena makes 3 paper triangles. How many corners in all?
qa.e: Each triangle has 3 corners. 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

qa.q: To make a paper dog face, what do we fold first?
qa.e: We fold a square into a triangle, then fold its corners down as ears.

qa.q: What shape does a round bottle cap print?
qa.e: The rim of the cap is round, so it prints a circle.

qa.q: Gita dips an eraser in paint and stamps it. What shape does she see?
qa.e: An eraser has a rectangle face, so it prints a rectangle.

qa.q: In the stamp pattern ○ □ ○ □ ○ ___, what comes next?
qa.e: Circle and square take turns. After a circle comes a square.

qa.q: Which of these is a pattern?
qa.a: red, green, red, green, red, green
qa.e: Red, green repeats in the same order every time.

qa.q: Sara prints a pattern: 🍃🍃✋🍃🍃✋. How many leaves are there?
qa.e: Each part has 2 leaves and 1 hand. 2 parts have 2 + 2 = 4 leaves.

qa.q: A mehndi pattern goes: dot, leaf, dot, leaf. What is the 5th design?
qa.e: 1st dot, 2nd leaf, 3rd dot, 4th leaf, 5th dot.

qa.q: A frog jumps on tiles: 1, 4, 7, 10. Which tile does it land on next?
qa.e: It adds 3 each time. 10 + 3 = 13.

qa.q: What is the rule in 1, 6, 11, 16?
Extend the pattern: 7, 14, 21, ___
qa.e: It adds 7 each time. 21 + 7 = 28.

qa.q: Extend the pattern: 1, 7, 13, ___
qa.e: It adds 6 each time. 13 + 6 = 19.

qa.q: In the tile pattern △ ○ ○ △ ○ ○ △ ___, what comes next?
qa.e: The part that repeats is △ ○ ○. After △ comes ○.

qa.q: Asha writes 3, 8, 13, 18. What does she write next?
qa.e: The rule is add 5. 18 + 5 = 23.

qa.q: In Tadasana you stand straight and tall. What line does your body make?
qa.e: Standing straight goes up and down. That is a standing line.

qa.q: Ajay lies flat on his back in Shavasana. What line does his body make?
qa.e: Lying flat goes side to side, like the floor. That is a sleeping line.

qa.q: In Trikonasana the legs spread wide apart. What lines do the legs make?
qa.e: Each leg leans to one side, so it makes a slanting line.

qa.q: In Bhujangasana (cobra pose) the back bends up. What line does the back make?
qa.e: A bent back is not straight. It makes a curved line.

qa.q: Which asana shows a sleeping line?
qa.e: In Shavasana you lie flat, making a sleeping line.

qa.q: Neha stretches both arms straight up over her head. What line do her arms make?
qa.e: Arms straight up go up and down, a standing line.

qa.q: A flagpole is a ___ line.
qa.e: A flagpole goes straight up and down. That is a standing line.

qa.q: Which line is like the floor of your room?
qa.e: The floor lies flat from left to right. That is a sleeping line.

qa.q: A slide in the park is a ___ line.
qa.e: A slide leans to one side. It is not straight up and not flat. So it is slanting.

qa.q: How many standing lines are in the letter H?
qa.e: H has a standing line on the left and one on the right. The middle line is sleeping.

qa.q: How many slanting lines are in the letter W?
qa.e: W goes down, up, down, up. Each part leans. That is 4 slanting lines.

qa.q: Which letter has only standing and sleeping lines?
qa.e: L has 1 standing line and 1 sleeping line. A, V and X have slanting lines.

qa.q: Which letter has only straight lines?
qa.e: T is made of 2 straight lines. O, C and S are curved.

qa.q: How many straight lines are in the letter T?
qa.e: T has 1 line on top and 1 line going down. That is 2 lines.

qa.q: Which shape is made of only one curved line?
qa.e: A circle is one round line that bends all the way. It has no straight lines.

qa.q: How many straight lines are in the letter E?
qa.e: E has 1 standing line on the left and 3 short lines going right. 1 + 3 = 4.

qa.q: Meena draws a smile on a face. What kind of line is a smile?
qa.e: A smile bends like a little bowl. So it is a curved line.

qa.q: How many curved lines are in the letter B?
qa.e: B has 1 straight line and 2 round bumps. Each bump is a curved line.

qa.q: Pari joins 4 dots to make a square. How many straight lines does she draw?
qa.e: A square has 4 sides, so she draws 4 lines.

qa.q: Om draws a square and puts 2 slanting lines on top for a roof. How many lines in all?
qa.e: 4 lines for the square and 2 for the roof. 4 + 2 = 6.

qa.q: Which kind of line do we use to draw a rainbow?
qa.e: A rainbow bends like an arch, so it is a curved line.

qa.q: A picture of a door is missing its right side. Which line is missing?
qa.e: The side of a door goes up and down. It is a standing line.

qa.q: A tent picture is missing one side of its roof. Which line should you trace?
qa.e: A tent roof leans to the side, so it is a slanting line.

qa.q: Riya draws a cloud with 5 bumps. Each bump is 1 curved line. How many curved lines?
qa.e: 5 bumps, each 1 curved line, make 5 curved lines.

qa.q: Meena draws a square. How many sleeping lines does it have?
qa.e: The top and the bottom of a square are sleeping lines. The two sides are standing lines.

qa.q: Kabir draws 2 triangles that do not touch. How many straight lines in all?
qa.e: Each triangle has 3 straight lines. 3 + 3 = 6.

qa.q: Which pattern repeats a curved line?
qa.e: ( bends, so it is a curved line. | and — are straight.

qa.q: What comes next? / \ / \ / ___
qa.e: The lines take turns: /, then \. After / comes \.

qa.q: Joseph makes a rangoli with 4 circles. How many curved lines?
qa.e: Each circle is 1 curved line. 4 circles make 4 curved lines.

qa.q: Aisha draws 2 squares and 1 triangle, none touching. How many straight lines?
qa.e: Squares: 4 + 4 = 8. Triangle: 3. 8 + 3 = 11.

qa.q: What is a zig-zag line made of?
qa.e: A zig-zag joins slanting lines, one going up and the next going down.

qa.q: A zig-zag goes up, down, up, down, up, down. How many slanting lines?
qa.e: Each up and each down is one line. 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

qa.q: A window has standing bars and sleeping bars. How many kinds of lines does it use?
qa.e: Standing and sleeping: that is 2 kinds of lines.

qa.q: Ali draws a hut with standing walls, a sleeping floor line and a slanting roof. Which line did he NOT use?
qa.e: He used standing, sleeping and slanting lines. No curved line.

qa.q: Which drawing uses a curved line?
qa.e: A rainbow is an arch, so it is curved. The others use straight lines only.

qa.q: Gauri draws 2 zig-zags. Each zig-zag has 4 slanting lines. How many slanting lines in all?
qa.e: 4 + 4 = 8 slanting lines.

qa.q: What kind of line does a flat fold in paper make?
qa.e: When you press a fold flat, the crease is a straight line.

qa.q: Bina folds a paper top edge to bottom edge and opens it. What kind of crease does she see?
qa.e: The crease goes from side to side across the paper. That is a sleeping line.

qa.q: Kabir folds a square paper corner to corner. What kind of crease does he get?
qa.e: A corner-to-corner crease leans across the square. It is slanting.

qa.q: Lila folds a paper 3 times, each time in a new place, opening it after each fold. How many creases?
qa.e: Each fold makes 1 crease. 3 folds make 3 creases.

qa.q: In a folding game, Raj makes 5 creases and Tanu makes 7. How many more creases did Tanu make?
qa.e: 7 - 5 = 2. Tanu made 2 more creases.

qa.q: Can you make a curved crease by folding paper flat?
qa.a: No, a flat fold makes a straight line
qa.e: However you fold it flat, the crease is always straight.

qa.q: Each garland has 10 flowers. How many flowers are in 6 garlands?
qa.e: Count in tens 6 times: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60.

qa.q: Asha uses 40 flowers to make garlands of 10. How many garlands did she make?
qa.e: 40 is 4 tens, so 4 garlands.

qa.q: Fill the table. Garlands: 1, 2, 3, 4. Flowers: 10, 20, 30, ___.
qa.e: Each garland adds 10 flowers. 30 + 10 = 40.

qa.q: Tina makes 2 garlands. Dev makes 5 garlands. How many flowers did they use in all?
qa.e: Tina used 20 and Dev used 50. 20 + 50 = 70.

qa.q: Gopal used 50 flowers and Sita used 30 flowers. How many flowers altogether?
qa.e: 5 tens and 3 tens make 8 tens. 50 + 30 = 80.

qa.q: Zara has made 9 garlands. She needs 10 garlands. How many more flowers does she need?
qa.e: She needs 1 more garland, and 1 garland has 10 flowers.

qa.q: On a ginladi, Rani moves 20 beads, then 15 more. How many beads did she move?
Start at 26 on a number line. Jump 10 forward. Where do you land?
qa.e: A jump of 10 adds 1 ten. 26 + 10 = 36.

qa.q: Om adds 34 + 23 on a number line. He jumps 10, 10 and then 3 ones from 34. Where does he land?
A number line shows jumps from 18 to 28 and then to 30. Which addition is it?
qa.e: 18 to 28 is a jump of 10. 28 to 30 is a jump of 2. 10 + 2 = 12.

qa.q: Use jumps to find 45 + 21.
qa.e: 45, 55, 65, then 1 more is 66.

qa.q: Kiran finds 52 + 4 by moving 4 more beads after 52. What is the total?
qa.e: Count on 4 from 52: 53, 54, 55, 56.

qa.q: Sonu has 3 rods and 4 cubes. Jaya has 2 rods and 5 cubes. How many blocks in all?
qa.e: Rods: 3 + 2 = 5 tens. Cubes: 4 + 5 = 9 ones. That is 59.

qa.q: In column addition, which column do we add first?
qa.e: We add the ones first, so we can carry a new ten if needed.

qa.q: Add in columns: 47 + 25
qa.e: Ones: 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 and carry 1. Tens: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7.

qa.q: In 38 + 46, the ones make 8 + 6 = 14. What do we write in the ones place?
qa.e: 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones. Write 4 and carry the 1 ten.

qa.q: Add in columns: 56 + 27
qa.e: Ones: 6 + 7 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Tens: 5 + 2 + 1 = 8.

qa.q: Add in columns: 61 + 28
qa.e: Ones: 1 + 8 = 9. Tens: 6 + 2 = 8. No carry needed.

qa.q: Riya has 24 diyas. Arjun has 13 diyas. How many diyas in all?
What is 52 + 30?
qa.e: 30 is 3 tens. 5 tens and 3 tens make 8 tens. The 2 ones stay. So 82.

qa.q: Kabir has 36 balloons. He buys 27 more. How many balloons now?
qa.e: Ones: 6 + 7 = 13. Write 3 and carry 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. So 63.

qa.q: What is 45 + 8?
Fill the gap: 40 + ___ = 70
qa.e: From 40, count on by 10s: 50, 60, 70. That is 3 tens, or 30.

qa.q: Which sum is equal to 50?
Ankit scored 43 runs in one match and 58 in the next. How many runs in all?
Priya had 26 pencils. She bought 15 more. How many pencils now?
qa.e: Ones: 6 + 5 = 11, carry 1. Tens: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. So 41.

qa.q: Raj has 48 marbles. He wins 36 more. How many marbles now?
qa.e: Ones: 8 + 6 = 14, carry 1. Tens: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. So 84.

qa.q: A bus has 52 people. 29 more get on. How many people are on the bus now?
qa.e: Ones: 2 + 9 = 11, carry 1. Tens: 5 + 2 + 1 = 8. So 81.

qa.q: Mummy spent ₹65 on fruit and ₹40 on milk. How much did she spend in all?
qa.e: 6 tens and 4 tens make 10 tens = 100. Then 5 more: 105.

qa.q: Which sum is more than 100?
qa.e: 76 + 25 = 101. The others are 99, 70 and 99.

qa.q: A rangoli has 25 red dots and 32 yellow dots. How many dots in all?
qa.e: 'In all' means add. Ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Tens: 2 + 3 = 5. So 57.

qa.q: There were 40 sweets in a box. The guests ate 18. How many sweets are left?
qa.e: 'Left' means take away. 0 is too small to take 8, so break a ten: 10 − 8 = 2. Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. So 22.

qa.q: Joseph's team scored 46 runs. The other team scored 38. How many more runs did Joseph's team score?
qa.e: 'How many more' means take the small number from the big one. 46 − 38 = 8.

qa.q: A train has 54 people. At a station, 21 get off. How many are on the train now?
qa.e: People got off, so take away. Ones: 4 − 1 = 3. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. So 33.

qa.q: Aisha buys a pencil for ₹15 and an eraser for ₹7. How much does she pay?
qa.e: She pays for both, so add. ₹15 + ₹5 = ₹20. Then 2 more makes ₹22.

qa.q: Which word in a story tells you to take away?
qa.e: 'Left' asks what remains after some are gone. So we take away.

qa.q: There are 10 diyas. The wind blows out 3. How many still glow?
qa.e: 10 take away 3 leaves 7.

qa.q: On a ginladi, Hari moves 25 beads. He pushes 5 back. How many are left?
qa.e: 25 take away 5 is 20.

qa.q: Start at 50 on a number line. Jump back 10. Where do you land?
qa.e: A jump back of 10 takes away 1 ten. 50 - 10 = 40.

qa.q: Find 57 - 23 by jumping back 10, 10 and then 3. Where do you land?
Jumps go back from 46 to 36, then to 33. Which subtraction is it?
qa.e: 46 to 36 is 10 back. 36 to 33 is 3 back. 10 + 3 = 13.

qa.q: Taking away means ___.
qa.e: When we take away, we find what is left.

qa.q: Show 37 with blocks. Take away 2 rods and 4 cubes. What is left?
qa.e: Rods: 3 - 2 = 1. Cubes: 7 - 4 = 3. 1 rod and 3 cubes is 13.

qa.q: Subtract in columns: 68 - 25
In 52 - 17, the ones are 2 - 7. What do we do first?
qa.e: 2 is less than 7, so break 1 ten. Now the ones are 12, and 12 - 7 = 5.

qa.q: Subtract in columns: 52 - 17
qa.e: Break a ten: 12 - 7 = 5. Tens: 4 - 1 = 3. So 35.

qa.q: Subtract in columns: 70 - 26
qa.e: Break a ten: 10 - 6 = 4. Tens: 6 - 2 = 4. So 44.

qa.q: Subtract in columns: 93 - 41
Harpreet made 45 laddoos. Her friends ate 12. How many laddoos are left?
qa.e: Ones: 5 − 2 = 3. Tens: 4 − 1 = 3. So 33 are left.

qa.q: What is 80 − 30?
qa.e: 8 tens take away 3 tens leaves 5 tens. 5 tens is 50.

qa.q: What is 52 − 27?
qa.e: 2 is too small to take 7. Break a ten: 12 − 7 = 5. Then 4 tens − 2 tens = 2 tens. So 25.

qa.q: Aisha had 30 bangles. She gave 8 to her sister. How many does Aisha have now?
qa.e: Count back 8 from 30: 29, 28, 27, 26, 25, 24, 23, 22. So 22 are left.

qa.q: Fill the gap: 90 − ___ = 50
qa.e: From 90 go back by 10s to 50: 80, 70, 60, 50. That is 4 tens, or 40.

qa.q: Kabir has 61 stickers. He uses 25. How many stickers are left?
qa.e: 1 is too small to take 5. Break a ten: 11 − 5 = 6. Then 5 tens − 2 tens = 3 tens. So 36.

qa.q: Arun had ₹82. He bought a kite for ₹22. How much money is left?
Lata had ₹60. She spent ₹20 on a ride. How much is left?
qa.e: 6 tens take away 2 tens leaves 4 tens. ₹40.

qa.q: Mira had 28 flowers. She gave 5 to her friend. How many are left?
qa.e: 28 - 5: ones 8 - 5 = 3, tens stay 2. So 23.

qa.q: A garland maker had 73 flowers. He gave 47 to the temple. How many are left?
qa.e: Break a ten: 13 - 7 = 6. Tens: 6 - 4 = 2. So 26.

qa.q: Neel had ₹78. He spent ₹24 on a book and ₹37 on colours. How much is left?
Sita had ₹50. After buying a toy she has ₹15 left. How much did the toy cost?
qa.e: Money spent = 50 - 15 = ₹35. Check: 35 + 15 = 50.

qa.q: Seema wants to skip 20 times. She has done 14 skips. How many more?
qa.e: Count on from 14 to 20: 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20. That is 6.

qa.q: There were 56 birds on a tree. More came, and now there are 87. How many birds came?
Tapan has tapped a drum 18 times. He wants 35 taps. How many more taps?
Fill the missing number: 42 + ___ = 60
A team needs 75 runs to win. They have 48. How many more runs do they need?
Kavi has 30 stickers. He wants 45. Which tells how many more he needs?
qa.e: The gap from 30 to 45 is found by 45 - 30 = 15.

qa.q: 30 + 20 = 50. Which subtraction fact is in the same family?
qa.e: Take away one part, 20, from the whole, 50, to get the other part, 30.
Changing the order does not change the sum. It is still 39.

qa.q: Fill the fact family: 47 + 22 = 69, so 69 - 22 = ___
qa.e: Take away one part from the whole to get the other part: 47.

qa.q: Fill the gap: 36 + ___ = 58
qa.e: From the family: 58 - 36 = 22. Check: 36 + 22 = 58.

qa.q: Which shows that changing the order does not change the sum?
qa.e: 18 + 7 and 7 + 18 are both 25.

qa.q: 40, 15 and 55 make a fact family. Which fact is NOT in it?
qa.e: 25 is not one of the numbers 40, 15, 55. The other three facts use only these numbers.

qa.q: In a pyramid, the two blocks below are 12 and 15. What is in the block above?
qa.e: Add the two blocks below: 12 + 15 = 27.

qa.q: In a pyramid, the top block is 40. One block below is 25. What is the other block below?
The bottom row of a pyramid is 10, 14, 6. What are the two middle blocks?
Bottom row 10, 14, 6 gives a middle row of 24 and 20. What is the top block?
Two blocks below are 35 and ___. The block above is 62. What is missing?
Bottom row 5, 8, 7. Middle row 13 and 15. What is the top block?
Raju wrote 46 + 37 = 73. What is the right answer?
qa.e: Ones: 6 + 7 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Tens: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. So 83.

qa.q: What mistake did Raju make in 46 + 37 = 73?
qa.e: The ones made 13. He wrote 3 but did not carry the 1 ten.

qa.q: Sana wrote 52 - 17 = 45. What is the right answer?
qa.e: Break a ten: 12 - 7 = 5. Tens: 4 - 1 = 3. So 35.

qa.q: Which mistake gives 52 - 17 = 45?
qa.a: Doing 7 - 2 instead of breaking a ten
qa.e: Doing 7 - 2 skips breaking a ten, so the tens stay 5 - 1 = 4. That gives 45. The right way: 12 - 7 = 5 and 4 - 1 = 3, so 35.

qa.q: Which sum is correct?
qa.e: Ones: 4 + 8 = 12, carry 1. Tens: 6 + 1 + 1 = 8. So 82.

qa.q: Ishan says 90 - 34 = 66. What is the right answer?
qa.e: Break a ten: 10 - 4 = 6. Tens: 8 - 3 = 5. So 56.

qa.q: Rahul measures his table with a book. It is 5 books long. His bed is 11 books long. Which is longer?
qa.e: 11 books is more than 5 books, so the bed is longer.

qa.q: A door is 9 books tall. A cupboard is 7 books tall. How many books taller is the door?
qa.e: 9 - 7 = 2 books.

qa.q: How should you place the books when you measure?
qa.a: End to end with no gaps
qa.e: Gaps would leave parts unmeasured. Place the units end to end.

qa.q: Isha traces her hand on squared paper. It is 7 squares long. Her brother's is 9 squares long. Whose hand is longer?
qa.e: 9 squares is more than 7 squares.

qa.q: A wall is 20 blocks long. Nisha has measured 12 blocks so far. How many more blocks to go?
qa.e: 20 - 12 = 8 more blocks.

qa.q: Raghav writes in his table: bed 12 books, door 9 books, mat 4 books. Which is the shortest?
qa.e: 4 books is the smallest count, so the mat is shortest.

qa.q: Path A to school is 8 boxes long. Path B is 5 boxes long. Which path is shorter?
qa.e: 5 boxes is less than 8 boxes, so Path B is shorter.

qa.q: Path X is 12 boxes, Path Y is 9 boxes and Path Z is 15 boxes. Which is the longest?
qa.e: 15 is the biggest number, so Path Z is the longest.

qa.q: Ravi takes a 7-box path. Gita takes a 10-box path. How many more boxes does Gita walk?
qa.e: 10 - 7 = 3 more boxes.

qa.q: You want to reach the shop quickly. Which path should you take?
qa.e: The shortest path takes the least time.

qa.q: Which line between two dots is the shortest?
qa.e: A straight line goes directly, so it is the shortest way.

qa.q: Meena walks 6 boxes to the park, then 4 more boxes to school. Arjun's path to school is 8 boxes. Whose path is shorter?
qa.e: Meena walks 6 + 4 = 10 boxes. 8 is less than 10, so Arjun's is shorter.

qa.q: A giraffe is 9 blocks tall. A camel is 7 blocks tall. Which is taller?
qa.e: 9 blocks is more than 7 blocks.

qa.q: How many blocks taller is a 9-block giraffe than a 7-block camel?
qa.e: 9 - 7 = 2 blocks.

qa.q: A monkey is 2 blocks, a goat 3 blocks and a camel 7 blocks tall. Which is the shortest?
qa.e: 2 is the fewest blocks, so the monkey is shortest.

qa.q: The camel is 7 blocks tall. The monkey is 2 blocks tall. How many blocks taller is the camel?
qa.e: 7 - 2 = 5 blocks.

qa.q: A horse is 6 blocks tall. A camel is 7 blocks tall. Is the horse taller or shorter?
qa.e: 6 is less than 7, so the horse is shorter.

qa.q: A 2-block monkey sits on top of a 7-block camel. How many blocks tall are they together?
qa.e: Stack the heights: 7 + 2 = 9 blocks.

qa.q: Arjun's book is 2 hand-spans long. His table is 7 hand-spans long. Which is longer?
qa.e: The table needs 7 spans and the book needs only 2. More spans means longer.

qa.q: Meena's mat is 5 spans long. Her rope is 9 spans long. How many spans longer is the rope?
qa.e: Find the difference. 9 − 5 = 4. The rope is 4 spans longer.

qa.q: What is the best way to measure the length of your classroom?
qa.e: A classroom is big. Steps are long, so counting is quick.

qa.q: Kabir walks across a room in 12 steps. His dad does it in 8 steps. Why?
qa.e: Dad's steps are longer. Longer steps cover the room in fewer steps.

qa.q: A table is 4 hand-spans long. Two such tables are put end to end. How many hand-spans long are they?
qa.e: Each table is 4 spans. 4 + 4 = 8 spans.

qa.q: Harpreet walks 6 steps to the door and 6 more steps to the gate. How many steps in all?
qa.e: Add the two parts. 6 + 6 = 12 steps.

qa.q: Which one is the heaviest?
qa.e: A brick is hard and solid. It is much heavier than a feather or a leaf.

qa.q: On a see-saw, Arjun goes down and Riya goes up. Who is heavier?
qa.e: The heavier side of a see-saw goes down. Arjun went down.

qa.q: A big balloon and a small stone. Which is heavier?
qa.e: The balloon is full of air and is very light. The small stone is heavier.

qa.q: On a balance, 1 melon weighs the same as 6 apples. 2 such melons weigh the same as how many apples?
qa.e: Each melon is 6 apples. 2 melons are 6 + 6 = 12 apples.

qa.q: A pencil balances 3 ₹1 coins. A pen balances 5 ₹1 coins. Which is heavier?
qa.e: The pen needs 5 coins to balance. 5 is more than 3, so the pen is heavier.

qa.q: A bag of onions balances 10 blocks. A bag of potatoes balances 14 blocks. How many more blocks for the potatoes?
qa.e: Find the difference. 14 − 10 = 4 more blocks.

qa.q: Fill in: A sheet of paper is ___ an eraser.
qa.e: A sheet of paper is thin and light. An eraser is a little heavier.

qa.q: Which is the heaviest: paper, eraser, pencil box or school bag?
qa.e: A school bag full of books is the heaviest.

qa.q: Which list goes from lightest to heaviest?
qa.a: Paper, eraser, pencil box, school bag
qa.e: It starts with the lightest, paper, and ends with the heaviest, the school bag.

qa.q: Tanvi holds a ball of cotton in one hand and an orange in the other. Which hand feels heavier?
qa.e: An orange is heavier than a small ball of cotton, so that hand is pulled down more.

qa.q: Fill in: A big pumpkin is ___ a small lemon.
qa.e: A big pumpkin weighs much more than a small lemon.

qa.q: Which of these is the lightest?
qa.e: A leaf weighs very little. The others are much heavier.

qa.q: On a balance, the left pan goes down and the right pan goes up. Which side is heavier?
qa.e: The heavier side always goes down.

qa.q: A bag of sand and a bag of dry leaves are the same size. Which is heavier?
qa.e: Same size does not mean same weight. Sand is much heavier.

qa.q: Both pans of a balance are level. What does it tell us?
qa.e: When the pans are level, the two sides weigh the same.

qa.q: On a balance, a brick goes down and a sponge goes up. How should you mark the sponge?
qa.e: The sponge went up, so it is the lighter one.

qa.q: Where can you check your own weight?
qa.e: A weighing machine shows how heavy we are.

qa.q: Ramu weighs 25 kg. His father weighs 70 kg. How much heavier is his father?
qa.e: 70 - 25 = 45. His father is 45 kg heavier.

qa.q: One glass of lemonade needs 2 spoons of sugar. How many spoons for 3 glasses?
qa.e: 2 spoons for each glass: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

qa.q: One glass needs 1 spoon of lemon juice. How many spoons for 4 glasses?
qa.e: 1 spoon for each of 4 glasses is 4 spoons.

qa.q: Riya used 10 spoons of sugar, 2 spoons for each glass. How many glasses did she make?
qa.e: Count in 2s to 10: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. That is 5 glasses.

qa.q: Tina's bottle fills 5 glasses. Om's bottle also fills 5 glasses. Which is true?
qa.e: Both fill 5 of the same glass, so they hold the same amount.

qa.q: Anu's bottle fills 7 glasses. Raj's bottle fills 4 glasses. How many more glasses does Anu's hold?
qa.e: 7 - 4 = 3 glasses more.

qa.q: Ben's bottle fills 3 glasses, Sia's fills 6 and Lali's fills 4. Whose bottle holds the least?
qa.e: 3 glasses is the smallest amount.

qa.q: Which one holds the most water?
qa.e: A bucket is much bigger inside. It can fill many cups.

qa.q: A jug fills 6 glasses. A bottle fills 4 glasses. How many more glasses does the jug fill?
qa.e: Find the difference. 6 − 4 = 2 more glasses.

qa.q: A pot fills 3 jugs. Each jug fills 5 glasses. How many glasses does the pot fill?
qa.e: 3 jugs of 5 glasses each. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15.

qa.q: Using the same cup, Kabir fills his bottle with 4 cups. Joseph fills his with 7 cups. Whose bottle holds more?
qa.e: Joseph's bottle takes 7 cups. 7 is more than 4, so it holds more.

qa.q: What does capacity mean?
qa.a: How much a thing can hold
qa.e: Capacity tells how much water, milk or sand a thing can hold.

qa.q: A bucket holds 10 mugs of water. Meena has poured in 6 mugs. How many more mugs to fill it?
qa.e: Count up from 6 to 10: 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 4 more mugs.

qa.q: Which one shows equal groups?
qa.e: In 3, 3, 3 every group has 3. The others have groups of different sizes.

qa.q: There are 5 plates. Each plate has 2 laddoos. How many laddoos?
qa.e: 5 groups of 2. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.

qa.q: Arjun makes 3 groups of 4 marbles. How many marbles?
qa.e: Count by 4s for 3 groups: 4, 8, 12.

qa.q: Meena puts 12 bangles in groups of 3. How many groups does she make?
qa.e: Count by 3s till 12: 3, 6, 9, 12. That is 4 groups.

qa.q: Three plates have 4, 4 and 3 sweets. How can we make the groups equal?
qa.a: Add 1 sweet to the last plate
qa.e: Add 1 to the last plate: 3 + 1 = 4. Now every plate has 4.

qa.q: Kabir has 4 boxes with 5 crayons in each. How many crayons?
qa.e: Count by 5s for 4 boxes: 5, 10, 15, 20.

qa.q: Which is the same as 4 + 4 + 4?
qa.e: There are 3 fours. 3 groups of 4 is 3 × 4.

qa.q: A cow has 4 legs. How many legs do 3 cows have?
qa.e: 3 groups of 4. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

qa.q: What is 5 + 5 + 5 + 5?
qa.e: Count by 5s four times: 5, 10, 15, 20.

qa.q: An auto has 3 wheels. How many wheels do 5 autos have?
qa.e: 5 groups of 3. Count by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15.

qa.q: 2 × 6 means ___
qa.e: 2 × 6 means 2 groups of 6. That is 6 + 6 = 12.

qa.q: Aisha has 2 Diwali boxes. Each box has 10 sweets. How many sweets?
A butterfly has 4 wings. How many wings do 5 butterflies have?
An octopus has 8 legs. How many legs do 2 octopuses have?
Soldiers stand in 4 rows. Each row has 5 soldiers. How many soldiers in all?
In a table, groups = 3 and number in each group = 6. What is the total?
Which multiplication matches 7 + 7 + 7?
qa.e: There are 3 sevens, so it is 3 groups of 7, or 3 × 7.

qa.q: A picture shows 2 groups of 6 stars. Which adding sentence matches it?
qa.e: 2 groups of 6 means 6 + 6 = 12.

qa.q: What is 7 × 2?
qa.e: Count in 2s seven times: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14.
Add 2 to 12 to get 14.

qa.q: What is 6 × 3?
qa.e: Count in 3s six times: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18.

qa.q: There are 4 tricycles. Each has 3 wheels. How many wheels?
Which number is in the table of 3?
9 children each have 2 hands. How many hands?
What is 8 × 5?
qa.e: Count in 5s eight times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40.

qa.q: How many fingers are on 7 hands?
qa.e: Each hand has 5 fingers. 7 × 5 = 35.

qa.q: What is 6 × 10?
qa.e: 6 tens make 60.

qa.q: Nikhil has 9 notes of ₹10. How much money is that?
Which number is NOT in the table of 5?
qa.e: Numbers in the table of 5 end in 5 or 0. 32 ends in 2.

qa.q: A packet has 5 biscuits. How many biscuits are in 4 packets?
4 groups of 3 make 12. How many do 3 groups of 4 make?
qa.e: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Turning the order around gives the same total.

qa.q: Which is the same as 5 × 4?
qa.e: Changing the order does not change the product: 5 × 4 = 4 × 5 = 20.

qa.q: A picture shows 4 rows of 6 flowers. How many flowers?
If 6 × 4 = 24, what is 4 × 6?
qa.e: The order does not change the answer. 4 × 6 = 24.

qa.q: Rani sees 2 rows of 7 tiles. Which two sentences fit?
qa.e: 2 rows of 7 is 14. Turned around, 7 rows of 2 is also 14.

qa.q: Which is true?
qa.e: Both are 15. The order does not matter in multiplication.

qa.q: Each packet has 5 bindis. How many bindis are in 8 packets?
A shirt has 6 buttons. How many buttons are on 4 shirts?
One pencil costs ₹4. How much do 6 pencils cost?
4 people sit in each car. How many people are in 3 cars?
A kite costs ₹10. Ravi buys 3 kites. How much does he pay?
Amma buys 2 boxes of 10 diyas each. How many diyas does she get?
3 × 2 = 6. Double it to find 3 × 4.
qa.e: Double 6 is 6 + 6 = 12. So 3 × 4 = 12.
Double 14 is 14 + 14 = 28.
Table of 8 = table of 2 + table of 6. 6 + 18 = 24.

qa.q: A hall has 4 rows of chairs with 5 chairs in each row. How many chairs?
qa.e: 4 rows of 5 is 4 × 5 = 20.

qa.q: Which multiplication fits an array of 2 rows and 7 columns?
qa.e: 2 rows with 7 in each row is 2 × 7 = 14.
8 is double 4, so 5 × 8 is double 20. 20 + 20 = 40.

qa.q: Riya shares 8 laddoos equally with her brother. How many does each get?
qa.e: 8 shared by 2 people. 4 + 4 = 8, so each gets 4.

qa.q: 15 pencils are shared equally by 3 children. How many does each child get?
qa.e: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15. So each child gets 5.

qa.q: Kabir gives away all his 12 stickers, 3 to each friend. How many friends get stickers?
qa.e: Make groups of 3 till 12: 3, 6, 9, 12. That is 4 friends.

qa.q: 20 children make 2 equal cricket teams. How many children are in each team?
qa.e: 10 + 10 = 20. So each team has 10 children.

qa.q: Joseph shares 7 sweets equally between 2 friends. What happens?
qa.a: Each gets 3 and 1 is left over
qa.e: 3 + 3 = 6. One sweet is left. 4 + 4 = 8 is too many.

qa.q: Meena gets 4 balloons. Her 2 friends get 4 balloons each too. How many balloons were shared?
qa.e: Meena and 2 friends make 3 children. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

qa.q: Sana draws 12 bindis equally on 2 ice-cream cones. How many on each cone?
qa.e: Share 12 between 2: 6 and 6. Check: 6 + 6 = 12.

qa.q: Two plates have 6 laddoos each. How many laddoos in all?
qa.e: 6 + 6 = 12 laddoos.

qa.q: 12 laddoos are put equally on 3 plates. How many on each plate?
qa.e: Give one to each plate again and again: 4, 4, 4. Check: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

qa.q: Two plates have 5 and 7 laddoos. Is this equal sharing?
qa.e: Equal sharing means every plate has the same number. 5 and 7 are not the same.

qa.q: Plates have 5 and 7 laddoos. How many should move from the 7-plate to make them equal?
qa.e: Move 1: then both plates have 6.

qa.q: Kiran sticks 15 bindis equally on 3 cards. How many on each card?
qa.e: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15, so each card gets 5.

qa.q: Tara has 21 beads. She puts 7 on each string. How many strings can she make?
qa.e: 21 - 7 = 14, 14 - 7 = 7, 7 - 7 = 0. She took 7 away 3 times.

qa.q: Rina has 20 flowers. She puts 5 in each vase. How many vases does she need?
qa.e: Count in 5s to 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 vases.

qa.q: 27 candles are packed equally in 3 boxes. How many candles are in each box?
qa.e: 9 + 9 + 9 = 27, so each box has 9.

qa.q: A shirt needs 6 buttons. How many shirts can 18 buttons go on?
qa.e: 6, 12, 18. That is 3 shirts.

qa.q: Arun takes 4 marbles away from 12 again and again till none are left. How many times does he do it?
3 × 5 = 15. So 15 sweets in packets of 5 make how many packets?
qa.e: 3 packets of 5 make 15, so 15 sweets fill 3 packets.

qa.q: Which season brings lots of rain?
qa.e: The monsoon is the rainy season in India.

qa.q: In which season do flowers bloom and new leaves grow?
qa.e: Spring is the season of new flowers and leaves.

qa.q: Holi is the festival of colours. In which season do we play Holi?
qa.e: Holi comes in March, in spring.

qa.q: Lohri is celebrated with a bonfire in January. Which season is it?
qa.e: January is cold, so it is winter. People sit around the warm fire.

qa.q: Kabir drinks lots of water and eats mangoes during his vacation. Which season is it?
qa.e: Mangoes and hot days mean summer.

qa.q: In which season does the weather turn pleasant and Diwali come?
qa.e: Diwali comes in October or November, in autumn.

qa.q: In which season do we wear sweaters?
qa.e: Winter is cold. Sweaters keep us warm.

qa.q: Aisha carries an umbrella and makes paper boats in puddles. Which season is it?
qa.e: Puddles and umbrellas mean lots of rain. It is the rainy season.

qa.q: On a calendar, the 1st is a Friday. What day is the 8th?
qa.e: The 8th is 7 days after the 1st. 7 days later is the same day: Friday.

qa.q: On a calendar, the 5th is a Tuesday. On which date is the next Tuesday?
qa.e: The next Tuesday is 7 days later. 5 + 7 = 12.

qa.q: Most months have how many days?
qa.e: Most months have 30 or 31 days. Only February has fewer.

qa.q: Which month is the shortest?
qa.e: February has only 28 days, or 29 in a leap year. Other months have 30 or 31.

qa.q: How many months are there in a year?
qa.e: January to December makes 12 months.

qa.q: Which month comes just after June?
qa.e: The order is May, June, July. So July comes after June.

qa.q: Which is the first month of the year?
qa.e: Every year starts with January.

qa.q: Which month comes just before January?
qa.e: December is the last month. Then a new year starts with January.

qa.q: Meena's birthday is in the 3rd month of the year. Which month is it?
qa.e: 1st January, 2nd February, 3rd March.

qa.q: How many months come after September in the same year?
qa.e: After September come October, November and December. That is 3 months.

qa.q: How many days are there in April?
qa.e: April is one of the 30-day months: April, June, September, November.

qa.q: How many days are there in December?
qa.e: December has 31 days.

qa.q: How many days does February have in a leap year?
qa.e: February has 28 days, and 1 more in a leap year: 29.

qa.q: How often does a leap year come?
qa.e: A leap year comes once every 4 years.

qa.q: 2024 was a leap year. Which year is the next leap year?
Which of these months has 30 days?
qa.e: September is a 30-day month. The others have 31 days.

qa.q: How many days are there in a week?
qa.e: Sunday to Saturday makes 7 days.

qa.q: Today is Thursday. What day is tomorrow?
qa.e: Tomorrow is the day after today. After Thursday comes Friday.

qa.q: Yesterday was Sunday. What day is today?
qa.e: Today is the day after yesterday. After Sunday comes Monday.

qa.q: Arjun plays cricket every Saturday and Sunday. How many days does he play in 2 weeks?
qa.e: He plays 2 days each week. 2 weeks: 2 + 2 = 4 days.

qa.q: How many days are there in 2 weeks?
qa.e: Each week has 7 days. 7 + 7 = 14 days.

qa.q: Kabir's birthday is 3 days after Monday. Which day is it?
qa.e: Count 3 days on from Monday: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday.

qa.q: The first Sunday of a 30-day month is the 2nd. What are the other Sundays?
qa.e: Add 7 each time: 2, 9, 16, 23, 30.

qa.q: A month of 31 days starts on a Sunday. How many Sundays does it have?
qa.e: Sundays: 1, 8, 15, 22, 29. That is 5 Sundays.

qa.q: A February has 28 days. How many Sundays does it have?
qa.e: 28 days is exactly 4 weeks, so there are 4 Sundays.

qa.q: In many schools, summer vacation is in which months?
qa.e: May and June are the hottest months, so schools close then.

qa.q: June has 30 days and July has 31 days. How many days in both months?
A month starts on a Monday. On which date is the first Sunday?
qa.e: Mon 1, Tue 2, Wed 3, Thu 4, Fri 5, Sat 6, Sun 7.

qa.q: How long does it take to clap once?
qa.e: A clap is very quick. It takes about a second.

qa.q: How long does it take to brush your teeth?
qa.e: Brushing takes about 2 or 3 minutes.

qa.q: Which of these takes hours?
qa.e: A school day lasts many hours. The others take seconds.

qa.q: Which takes longer: drinking a glass of milk or sleeping at night?
qa.e: Sleeping takes many hours. Drinking milk takes a minute or two.

qa.q: Which of these can take days?
qa.a: A long train trip across India
qa.e: A train trip across India can take 2 days.

qa.q: Which takes less time: sneezing or taking a bath?
qa.e: A sneeze takes a second. A bath takes minutes.

qa.q: Asha stays with her Nani from 24 to 28 November. How many days is her trip?
qa.e: Count every day: 24, 25, 26, 27, 28. That is 5 days.

qa.q: The school picnic leaves at 8 o'clock in the morning and returns at 2 o'clock. How many hours?
qa.e: 8 to 12 is 4 hours. 12 to 2 is 2 hours. 4 + 2 = 6.

qa.q: A family leaves at 9 o'clock in the morning for a 5-hour trip. When do they get back?
qa.e: 9 to 12 is 3 hours. 2 more hours makes 2 o'clock.

qa.q: Train A takes 12 hours. Train B takes 9 hours. Which journey took longer?
qa.e: 12 hours is more than 9 hours.

qa.q: How many more hours did a 12-hour train journey take than a 9-hour one?
qa.e: 12 - 9 = 3 hours more.

qa.q: Vikram's trip is from 1 to 3 January. How many days is it?
qa.e: 1, 2, 3. That is 3 days.

qa.q: Which hand on a clock tells the hour?
qa.e: The short hand is the hour hand.

qa.q: The long hand is on 12 and the short hand is on 7. What time is it?
qa.e: Long hand on 12 means o'clock. The short hand shows 7.

qa.q: The short hand is on 10 and the long hand is on 12. What time does the clock show?
qa.e: The short hand gives the hour: 10. Long hand on 12 means o'clock.

qa.q: The long hand points to 12. What does that tell you?
qa.e: When the minute hand is on 12, the time is an exact hour, like 3 o'clock.

qa.q: At about what time do many children eat lunch?
qa.e: Lunch is in the afternoon, at about 1 o'clock.

qa.q: Which hand on a clock is the minute hand?
qa.e: The long hand is the minute hand.

qa.q: The short hand is on 3 and the long hand is on 12. What time is it?
qa.e: The short hand shows the hour, 3.

qa.q: To show 6 o'clock, where does the short hand go?
qa.e: The short hand points to the hour, 6.

qa.q: To show 6 o'clock, where does the long hand go?
qa.e: For any o'clock time the long hand points to 12.

qa.q: Om wakes up at 6 o'clock. School starts 2 hours later. What time does school start?
qa.e: 6 + 2 = 8. School starts at 8 o'clock.

qa.q: Both hands point to 12. What time is it?
qa.e: Short hand on 12 and long hand on 12 shows 12 o'clock.

qa.q: Meera goes to bed at 9 o'clock. Where are the clock hands?
qa.a: Short hand on 9, long hand on 12
qa.e: The short hand shows the hour, 9. The long hand is on 12.

qa.q: In which direction does the sun rise?
qa.e: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.

qa.q: On a map, which direction is usually at the top?
qa.e: Maps usually show north at the top.

qa.q: On a map, the well is to the right of the temple. In which direction is the well from the temple?
qa.e: On a map, right is east.

qa.q: Which direction is opposite to east?
qa.e: East and west are opposites.

qa.q: The library is north of Ravi's house. Where is Ravi's house from the library?
qa.e: North and south are opposites, so the house is south of the library.

qa.q: Tina walks north to the gate, then turns and walks east to the shop. In which direction did she walk last?
qa.e: First she went north, then east. The last part was east.

qa.q: A balloon costs ₹15. A whistle costs ₹10. How much for both?
qa.e: Add the prices. ₹15 + ₹10 = ₹25.

qa.q: Kabir has a ₹50 note and a ₹20 note. How much money does he have?
qa.e: ₹50 + ₹20: 5 tens and 2 tens make 7 tens. That is ₹70.

qa.q: What is ₹45 + ₹27?
qa.e: Ones: 5 + 7 = 12. Write 2, carry 1. Tens: 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. So ₹72.

qa.q: Harpreet buys a toffee for ₹2, a pencil for ₹5 and a pen for ₹10. How much does she pay?
Joseph has three ₹10 coins and four ₹1 coins. How much money does he have?
qa.e: Three ₹10 coins make ₹30. Four ₹1 coins make ₹4. ₹30 + ₹4 = ₹34.

qa.q: Riya saves ₹20 on Monday and ₹20 on Tuesday. How much does she save in all?
qa.e: ₹20 + ₹20: 2 tens and 2 tens make 4 tens. That is ₹40.

qa.q: Raju had ₹40. After a ride, he has ₹37 left. How much did the ride cost?
A toy train ride costs ₹15 and a balloon costs ₹5. How much money is needed for both?
Gita has ₹43. Her mother gives her ₹14 more. How much does she have now?
qa.e: More means add: 43 + 14 = 57.

qa.q: Leela had ₹50. She has ₹18 left after the fair. How much did she spend?
qa.e: Spent = 50 - 18. Break a ten: 10 - 8 = 2, tens 4 - 1 = 3. So ₹32.

qa.q: Candy floss costs ₹12 more than a ₹20 ride. What does the candy floss cost?
Sam wants a ₹25 ride and a ₹10 snack. How much money does he need?
qa.e: Add the prices: 25 + 10 = ₹35.

qa.q: How many ₹1 coins make ₹10?
qa.e: Each coin is ₹1. Count 1 to 10. That is 10 coins.

qa.q: Riya has two ₹10 notes and one ₹5 coin. How much money does she have?
How many ₹5 coins make ₹20?
qa.e: Count by 5s till 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 coins.

qa.q: Which is the most money?
qa.e: ₹50 is more than ₹20 and ₹10.

qa.q: Arjun has one ₹50 note. Kabir has five ₹10 notes. Who has more money?
qa.e: Five ₹10 notes: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. That is ₹50, same as Arjun.

qa.q: Meena has three ₹20 notes. How much money does she have?
qa.e: Count by 20s: 20, 40, 60. That is ₹60.

qa.q: Which monument is on the back of the ₹500 note?
qa.e: The ₹500 note shows the Red Fort in Delhi.

qa.q: How is 500 written in words on the note?
qa.e: 500 is five hundreds, so it is Five Hundred Rupees.

qa.q: A note says 'One Hundred Rupees'. How much is it in numbers?
qa.e: One hundred is written as 100.

qa.q: Whose picture is on the front of Indian notes?
qa.e: Gandhiji's picture is on the front of our notes.

qa.q: Ravi sees 'Twenty Rupees' on a note. How much is the note?
qa.e: Twenty is written as 20.

qa.q: Which is worth more: a ₹500 note or a ₹200 note?
qa.e: 500 is more than 200.

qa.q: How many paise make 1 rupee?
qa.e: 1 rupee is 100 paise.

qa.q: How many 25-paise coins make 1 rupee?
qa.e: 25, 50, 75, 100. That is 4 coins.

qa.q: How many 20-paise coins make 1 rupee?
Dadi has three 25-paise coins. How many paise is that?
Which coins make exactly 1 rupee?
Two 50-paise coins make how many paise?
qa.e: 50 + 50 = 100 paise, which is ₹1.

qa.q: Tara pops balloons with ₹10, ₹5 and ₹2. How much does she win?
Balloons show ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20. Which two make ₹25?
Balloons show ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20. With 3 chances, what is the most you can win?
qa.e: Pop the three biggest: 20 + 10 + 5 = 35.

qa.q: Balloons show ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 and ₹20. With 4 chances, what is the most you can win?
qa.e: Pop the four biggest: 20 + 10 + 5 + 2 = 37.

qa.q: Arun wants to win exactly ₹12. Which balloons should he pop?
qa.e: 10 + 2 = 12. The others make 10, 11 and 7.

qa.q: Mina won ₹20 and ₹5. Her brother won ₹10, ₹10 and ₹2. Who won more?
qa.e: Mina: 20 + 5 = 25. Brother: 10 + 10 + 2 = 22. 25 is more.

qa.q: Which set makes ₹66?
qa.e: 50 + 10 + 5 + 1 = 66. The others make 71, 65 and 65.

qa.q: Another way to make ₹66 is ₹20 + ₹20 + ₹20 + ₹5 + ___. What is missing?
qa.e: 20 + 20 + 20 + 5 = 65. One more rupee makes 66.

qa.q: What is the fewest number of notes and coins to pay ₹30?
qa.e: ₹20 + ₹10 = ₹30. That is 2 notes. There is no ₹30 note.

qa.q: Which set pays ₹38 with the fewest notes and coins?
qa.e: All three make ₹38. The second set uses only 5 pieces; the other two use 6.

qa.q: Ria pays ₹45 with some ₹20 notes and one ₹5 coin. How many ₹20 notes does she use?
qa.e: 45 - 5 = 40, and 40 is two ₹20 notes.

qa.q: Which is the fewest notes to pay ₹150?
qa.e: ₹100 + ₹50 uses just 2 notes.

qa.q: A kite costs ₹15. Arjun pays ₹20. How much change does he get?
qa.e: Change = ₹20 − ₹15. Count up from 15 to 20: that is 5. So ₹5.

qa.q: Aisha has ₹30. A doll costs ₹25. Can she buy it?
qa.e: ₹30 is more than ₹25, so she can buy it. ₹30 − ₹25 = ₹5 change.

qa.q: Kabir pays ₹50 for a toy car that costs ₹35. How much change does he get?
Joseph has ₹40. He buys a ball for ₹18. How much money is left?
A stall sells laddoos at ₹5 each. How much for 4 laddoos?
qa.e: 4 laddoos at ₹5 each. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. So ₹20.

qa.q: Riya wants a ₹60 bag. She has ₹45. How much more money does she need?
Colour Day table: Red 7, Blue 4, Green 5, Yellow 2. Which colour is most liked?
qa.e: Red has the biggest number, 7.

qa.q: In the table Red 7, Blue 4, Green 5, Yellow 2, which colour is least liked?
qa.e: Yellow has the smallest number, 2.

qa.q: 7 children wear red and 4 wear blue. How many more wear red than blue?
qa.e: 7 - 4 = 3 more.

qa.q: Fruit table: Mango 6, Apple 3, Banana 6. Which is true?
qa.e: Mango and banana both have 6, so they are equal.

qa.q: Count and fill the table: 🍇🍇🍇🍇🍇. How many children like grapes?
qa.e: There are 5 grape pictures, so 5 children.

qa.q: Fruit table: Mango 6, Apple 3, Banana 6, Guava 2. How many children in all?
Arjun sorts 10 marbles. 6 are red and the rest are blue. How many are blue?
qa.e: The rest means what is left. 10 − 6 = 4 blue marbles.

qa.q: In a class, 7 children like cricket and 5 like football. How many children in all?
qa.e: 'In all' means add. 7 + 5 = 12.

qa.q: 7 children like cricket and 5 like football. How many more children like cricket?
qa.e: 'How many more' means find the difference. 7 − 5 = 2.

qa.q: Meena puts her red toys in one box and her blue toys in another. What is she doing?
qa.e: Putting things into groups by colour is sorting.

qa.q: Kabir asks 9 friends. 4 like mango, 3 like apple and 2 like banana. Which fruit is liked the least?
qa.e: Banana has only 2. That is the smallest number.

qa.q: Aisha has 3 red, 5 yellow and 4 green bangles. How many bangles in all?
Kabir counts cars at the gate. His tally is |||. How many cars?
qa.e: Each line is 1. There are 3 lines, so the number is 3.

qa.q: How do we make a bundle of 5 in tally marks?
qa.a: We draw a line across 4 lines
qa.e: We draw 4 lines. The 5th line goes across them. That is a bundle of 5.

qa.q: Riya's tally shows 3 bundles. How many is that?
qa.e: Each bundle is 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15.

qa.q: Joseph's tally shows 2 bundles and |||| (4 lines). How many is that?
qa.e: 2 bundles: 5, 10. Then 4 more: 11, 12, 13, 14.

qa.q: How do we show 7 with tally marks?
qa.e: 1 bundle is 5. 5 and 2 more make 7. So 1 bundle and ||.

qa.q: Aisha's bird tally shows 1 bundle and |. Then 3 more birds come. How many birds now?
qa.e: 1 bundle and | is 5 + 1 = 6. Then 3 more: 6 + 3 = 9.

qa.q: In a pictograph, each 🙂 stands for 1 child. 6 children walk to school. How many faces go in the Walk row?
qa.e: One face for each child, so 6 faces.

qa.q: Table: Bus 5, Walk 3, Cycle 4, Car 2. How many children were asked?
Bus row: 🙂🙂🙂🙂🙂. Car row: 🙂🙂. How many more children come by bus than by car?
qa.e: 5 - 2 = 3 more.

qa.q: Why should all the faces in a pictograph be the same size?
qa.a: So we can compare the rows fairly
qa.e: If some faces are bigger, a short row could look longer. Same size keeps it fair.

qa.q: Riya draws the Cycle row with 4 faces. How many children come by cycle?
qa.e: Each face is one child, so 4 faces mean 4 children.

qa.q: What do we do first, before drawing the pictograph?
qa.e: We first count each group and fill the table. Then we draw the faces.

qa.q: Pictograph (each picture = 1 child): Laddoo 🟡🟡🟡🟡🟡, Jalebi 🟠🟠🟠. How many children like laddoo?
qa.e: Count the pictures in the laddoo row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

qa.q: Each picture = 1 child. Laddoo 🟡🟡🟡🟡🟡, Jalebi 🟠🟠🟠. How many more children like laddoo than jalebi?
qa.e: Laddoo 5, Jalebi 3. 5 − 3 = 2 more.

qa.q: Pets: Dog 🐶🐶🐶🐶, Cat 🐱🐱, Fish 🐟🐟🐟. Which pet do the most children have?
qa.e: The dog row has 4 pictures. That is the most.

qa.q: Pets: Dog 🐶🐶🐶🐶, Cat 🐱🐱, Fish 🐟🐟🐟. How many pets in all?
In a pictograph, each ⭐ means 1 child. The cricket row has 7 stars. How many children chose cricket?
qa.e: Each star is 1 child. 7 stars means 7 children.

qa.q: Trip pictograph: Bus 🚌🚌🚌, Train 🚆🚆🚆🚆🚆🚆, Car 🚗🚗. Which is liked the least?
qa.e: The car row has only 2 pictures. That is the fewest.

qa.q: Face chart: Cricket 8, Kho-kho 5, Kabaddi 3, Football 6. Which game is liked the most?
qa.e: Cricket has the most faces, 8.

qa.q: Face chart: Cricket 8, Kho-kho 5, Kabaddi 3, Football 6. Which game is liked the least?
qa.e: Kabaddi has the fewest faces, 3.

qa.q: 6 children like football and 3 like kabaddi. How many more like football?
qa.e: 6 - 3 = 3 more.

qa.q: 8 children chose cricket and 5 chose kho-kho. How many chose these two games in all?
Kabaddi has 🙂🙂🙂🙂 and kho-kho has 🙂🙂🙂🙂. Which is true?
qa.e: Both rows have 4 faces, so they are equal.

qa.q: In a face chart, the cricket row has 9 faces. How many children like cricket?
qa.e: One face for each child: 9 faces, 9 children.

qa.q: Vegetable survey: Potato 9, Carrot 4, Peas 6, Bhindi 5. Which is the most liked?
qa.e: Potato has the biggest number, 9.

qa.q: Vegetable survey: Potato 9, Carrot 4, Peas 6, Bhindi 5. How many children were asked in all?
Family sizes of friends: 4, 3, 5, 4, 6, 4. Which family size is the most common?
qa.e: 4 comes three times. The others come once.

qa.q: Family sizes: 4, 3, 5, 4, 6, 4. How many members does the smallest family have?
qa.e: The smallest number in the list is 3.

qa.q: Family sizes: 4, 3, 5, 4, 6, 4. How many families have more than 4 members?
qa.e: Only 5 and 6 are more than 4. That is 2 families.

qa.q: What is a survey?
qa.a: Asking many people the same question
qa.e: In a survey we ask many people one question and record their answers.

qa.q: What should you do before you start a survey?
qa.e: Planning the questions tells you what to ask and what to record.

qa.q: Which is a clear survey question?
qa.a: Do your grandparents live with you?
qa.e: It is short and has a clear answer.

qa.q: Table: Both 4, One 3, None 5. How many families have no grandparents at home?
qa.e: The None row shows 5.

qa.q: Table: Both 4, One 3, None 5. How many families were asked in all?
Table: Both 4, One 3, None 5. How many families have one or both grandparents at home?
qa.e: Both 4 + One 3 = 7.

qa.q: Table: Both 6, One 2, None 1. Which group is the biggest?
qa.e: 6 is the biggest number.

qa.q: I have 3 sides and 3 corners. Who am I?
qa.e: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.

qa.q: I have no corners and no edges, and I can roll. Who am I?
qa.e: A sphere is curved all over, so it has no corners or edges.

qa.q: Which object can make a circle shadow?
qa.e: A ball is round from every side, so its shadow is a circle.

qa.q: How many matchsticks do you need to make 2 squares that do not touch?
qa.e: Each square needs 4 sticks. 4 + 4 = 8.

qa.q: Two squares share one side. How many matchsticks are needed?
qa.e: 8 sticks for two squares, but one side is shared. 8 - 1 = 7.

qa.q: A big square of 12 matchsticks has 4 small squares inside. Take away the 4 inside sticks. How many squares are left?
qa.e: Only the outside is left, and it is 1 big square.

qa.q: In a join-the-pairs puzzle, you join each shape to its matching shape. What must be true about the lines?
qa.a: They must not cross each other
qa.e: The puzzle is to join every pair so that no two lines cross.

qa.q: How do we write 17 in words?
qa.e: 17 is seven more than ten: seventeen.

qa.q: Which number is 'nineteen'?
qa.e: Nineteen is 1 ten and 9 ones: 19.

qa.q: Complete the pattern: 11, 22, 33, ___
qa.e: Each number adds 11. 33 + 11 = 44.

qa.q: Using only the digit 8, which 2-digit number can you make?
qa.e: Put 8 in both places: 88.

qa.q: How many 2-digit numbers have both digits the same, like 11 and 22?
Complete the pattern: 2, 4, 6, ___, 10
qa.e: The pattern adds 2. 6 + 2 = 8.

qa.q: Which number has a double of 18?
qa.e: Double 9 is 9 + 9 = 18. So the number is 9, half of 18.

qa.q: Try the trick with 5: double it (10), add 8 (18), take half (9), take away 5. What do you get?
qa.e: 9 - 5 = 4. The trick always ends in 4!

qa.q: Do the trick with 7. What is the final answer?
qa.e: Double 7 = 14, add 8 = 22, half = 11, take away 7 = 4.

qa.q: Using only the keys 5, + and =, how many times must you press 5 to make 20?
qa.e: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20. That is 4 fives.

qa.q: Using only the keys 2, + and =, which number can you NOT make?
qa.e: Adding 2s gives 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 ... only even numbers. 7 is odd.

qa.q: What is half of 14?
qa.e: 7 + 7 = 14, so half of 14 is 7.

qa.q: Which two numbers add up to 30?
qa.e: 18 + 12 = 30. The others make 25, 32 and 25.
7 is smaller than 12, so take away: 12 - 5 = 7.
14 is bigger than 8, so add: 8 + 6 = 14.

qa.q: From 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25, which three numbers add to 30?
qa.e: 5 + 10 + 15 = 30. The others make 50 and 45.

qa.q: Star puzzle: 4 is in the middle and each line must add to 12. Which number goes on the line with 1?
Star puzzle: 4 is in the middle and each line adds to 12. Which number goes on the line with 2?
3 roads go from home to the shop. 2 roads go from the shop to school. How many ways from home to school?
qa.e: Each of the 3 roads can be followed by 2 roads: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

qa.q: 1 road goes from Riya's house to the park. 4 roads go from the park to the lake. How many ways to the lake?
qa.e: She must take the one road, then any of the 4 roads. That is 4 ways.

qa.q: In a maze, Ravi's path passes 3 bananas and 2 apples. He picks them all. How many fruits does he get?
qa.e: 3 + 2 = 5 fruits.

qa.q: In a maze, what should you do at a dead end?
qa.a: Go back and try another way
qa.e: A dead end has no way out, so go back and try a different path.

qa.q: A garden has 6 trees. The gardener divides it into 3 equal parts. How many trees are in each part?
qa.e: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6, so each part has 2 trees.

qa.q: A box of 12 crayons is split into 4 equal parts. How many crayons are in each part?
A 6 m cloth is cut into 1 m pieces. How many cuts are needed?
qa.e: 6 pieces need 1 cut fewer: 6 - 1 = 5 cuts.

qa.q: How many pieces do 3 cuts make in a straight ribbon?
qa.e: Each cut adds 1 piece. 3 cuts make 3 + 1 = 4 pieces.

qa.q: A log is cut into 8 pieces. How many cuts were made?
qa.e: 8 pieces need 8 - 1 = 7 cuts.

qa.q: 4 dots sit like the corners of a square. You join them. How many rectangles do you get?
qa.e: Joining the 4 corner dots makes 1 square, and a square is a rectangle.

qa.q: Dots are in 2 rows of 3. Joining dots, how many rectangles can you make, counting squares too?
qa.e: 2 small squares and 1 long rectangle: 2 + 1 = 3.

qa.q: Dots in 2 rows of 3 make how many small squares?
qa.e: Each small square uses 4 dots side by side. There are 2 of them.
